title: A few useful IntelliJ shortcuts
answer: A few IntelliJ shortcuts I use on the default Windows/Linux keymap are: double Shift for Search Everywhere, Ctrl+Shift+N for Go to File, Ctrl+E for Recent Files, Ctrl+B for Go to Declaration, Alt+F7 for Find Usages, Ctrl+F12 for File Structure, Ctrl+Q for Quick Documentation, and Alt+Enter for intention actions and quick fixes. These shortcuts reduce mouse-driven navigation and help me move between files, symbols, usages, documentation, and fixes quickly. Shortcut keys can differ by operating system or custom keymap, so I verify the active IntelliJ keymap when working on a different setup.

steps.title: Use Search Everywhere — double Shift
steps.question: Search Everywhere reduces the need to navigate menus or project-tree folders first; you can start from what you remember about the target. IntelliJ can search classes, files, symbols, settings, and actions from one entry point. Why is double Shift a useful first shortcut to remember when you do not know exactly where something lives?
steps.why: Search Everywhere reduces the need to navigate menus or project-tree folders first; you can start from what you remember about the target.

steps.title: Use Go to File — Ctrl+Shift+N
steps.question: Go to File searches by filename and lets you jump directly to the target without manually traversing the package tree. When you know a filename but not its folder path, why is Ctrl+Shift+N faster than expanding several project-tree directories?
steps.why: Go to File searches by filename and lets you jump directly to the target without manually traversing the package tree.

steps.question: File Structure lists the symbols inside the current file and lets you jump to the member you need. A long Java class can contain many methods and fields. Why is Ctrl+F12 useful when you want to move inside one file without scrolling through every line?

steps.title: Use intention actions — Alt+Enter
steps.question: Intention actions surface relevant fixes or improvements exactly where the IDE detects a problem or opportunity. IntelliJ can suggest imports, fixes, and context-aware transformations at the caret. Why is Alt+Enter one of the most useful shortcuts to know? The Use intention actions — Alt+Enter action exposes the relevant IntelliJ state directly, so the question stays tied to observable project behavior rather than generic interview wording.
